headline: Thanksgiving's storm brings strong to damaging winds and heavy rain to New York City, peaking late this afternoon into evening, along with widespread moderate coastal flooding at both of Thursday's high tides, with Thursday evening's tide now expected to be the higher one.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A storm moving north from the Mid-Atlantic, squeezed against strong high pressure over the Northeast, brings strong to damaging east-northeast winds and rain to New York City on Thanksgiving. Winds build to about 25 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph this morning, then reach about 30 to 40 mph with gusts of roughly 45 to 58 mph in the afternoon, strongest in the city and along the coast, with the peak most likely late afternoon into evening (possibly 1 to 3 hours later than forecast). A High Wind Warning runs from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for the city, Long Island and the nearby New Jersey waterfront, with a Wind Advisory from 10 AM to 5 AM Friday farther north and west and in Connecticut; gusts near 58 mph are possible along coastal Connecticut and southern Westchester, and isolated gusts that strong in eastern Bergen County. The heaviest rain comes late afternoon into evening with a rumble of thunder possible, mainly causing minor street and poor-drainage flooding, though there is a slight chance of flash flooding in the city; rain and wind ease late tonight as winds turn southeast to south.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday brings a chance of light rain or showers, mainly north and west of the city, with the storm still nearby and a breezy southwest wind gusting about 30 to 35 mph that turns west after midnight. High pressure brings dry weather Saturday, with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph that ease Saturday night. The discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday stays dry, then showers are likely after midnight Sunday night. A chance of showers lingers Monday morning, with southwest gusts around 25 to 30 mph turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. The discussion gives no detail beyond Monday.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday morning into Thursday night, on top of already-high tides after the recent full moon, make widespread moderate coastal flooding likely at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with locally major flooding possible mainly in southern Nassau and southwest Suffolk along the western Great South Bay, and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. The surge now lines up better with Thursday evening's high tide, which will likely be the higher of the two, especially along Long Island Sound, and heavy rain at that time could worsen coastal street flooding; forecasters leaned toward the higher-end water levels for a safety margin. Coastal Flood Warnings run until 6 AM Friday, followed by Coastal Flood Advisories for Friday morning's high tide, when winds turn southwest and impacts should be minor to locally moderate; a Coastal Flood Watch remains for Long Island's south shore, though confidence in moderate flooding there has dropped. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breakers with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash flooding roads and structures behind the dunes; western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Storm Warning runs until 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas near 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves near 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and likely below that Sunday, with small-craft conditions possible again Monday, especially on the ocean.
watch_for: Peak winds late Thursday afternoon and evening, possibly arriving 1 to 3 hours later than forecast
Thursday evening's high tide, now expected to be the higher one, coinciding with heavy rain
Friday morning's high tide on Long Island's south shore, under a Coastal Flood Watch
confidence: Forecasters are confident the strongest winds come late Thursday afternoon into evening but some timing disagreement remains, the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end, and confidence in moderate flooding at Friday morning's tide has dropped.
